name: Rajma Masala
description: Homestyle rajma masala with tender red kidney beans simmered in a well-cooked onion-tomato masala until the gravy is thick enough to cling to each bean.
ingredients: 2 cans (400 g each) cooked red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
½ tsp red chilli powder, or to taste
¾ cup water, plus a little more if needed
¾ tsp salt, or to taste
method: Drain and rinse the canned kidney beans. If substituting dried kidney beans, soak and boil them thoroughly until fully tender before using them in the masala; do not use raw or undercooked kidney beans.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat and cook the chopped onion patiently until soft and deep golden without burning.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir briefly, then add the chopped tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook while pressing the tomatoes until the mixture becomes thick and cohesive.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric and red chilli powder and cook briefly, adding a small splash of water only if the spices begin sticking to the pan.
Add the cooked kidney beans, measured water and salt. Bring to a simmer and cook gently uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the beans absorb flavour and the gravy reduces.
Mash a small spoonful of beans against the side of the pan and stir them back in to thicken the gravy naturally. Adjust with a little hot water if the consistency becomes too heavy.
Turn off the heat, stir in the garam masala, taste for salt and chilli and finish with fresh coriander. Serve with lemon wedges, rice or chapati.
tips: Canned beans save the overnight soak; rinse them well so their liquid does not make the gravy taste too salty.
Cook the onion and tomatoes until thick before adding the beans; this gives the masala body without cream.
For a thicker sauce, mash a small portion of the beans rather than adding flour.
storage: Cool leftover rajma promptly and refrigerate covered. Reheat only the portion needed until thoroughly hot, adding a splash of water if the gravy has thickened.
serving: Spoon over plain rice, or serve with chapati, a little plain yogurt and sliced onion.
